title: Ranked Match Tilt Sequence Detector
dataSources: Game sessions (`game:session`), ranked matches (`ranked:match`), co-op invites (`coop:session`), speedrun attempts (`speedrun:attempt`), server events (`server:event`), board-game plays (`boardgame:play`), raid attempts (`raid:attempt`), and daily quest logs (`quest:completion`).
app: Gaming telemetry from platform session APIs, ranked-match exports, co-op schedulers, speedrun splits, server logs, raid trackers, and board-game play records streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=ranked:match
| sort 0 _time
| streamstats current=f last(result) as prev_result by player game
| eval tilt_loss=if(prev_result="loss" AND result="loss",1,0)
| stats sum(tilt_loss) as back_to_back_losses by player game
| sort - back_to_back_losses
description: Counts back-to-back loss sequences in ranked play so tilt-prone stretches are easier to recognize.
value: A sequence view helps you spot when performance problems are clustering rather than being random ups and downs.
implementation: Ingest ranked results chronologically for each player and game, then count repeated-loss chains.
visualization: Bar chart of back-to-back loss sequences by player and game.
grandmaExplanation: It watches when losing streaks start piling up in ranked play instead of staying occasional.
